name: apple-hig
description: Use when designing, implementing, or reviewing interfaces for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, watchOS, CarPlay, or other Apple system experiences using Apple's Human Interface Guidelines. Routes to current platform, foundation, pattern, component, input, and technology guidance.
license: MIT
metadata:

  source: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines

# Apple Human Interface Guidelines

Use the relevant Apple guidance to make concrete design decisions. This package
contains a router, 13 family routes, 158 operational topic skills, and supporting
article-level references. It is
independent of Apple. The sources are a dated English HIG snapshot; check the
official source when a task depends on a newer release or a disputed detail.

## Route the task

1. Identify the target platform, device context, and user task from the request or
   project. Ask for the platform only when it materially affects the answer and
   cannot be inferred. Preserve the user's framework and product requirements.
2. Select the relevant family below and read that family's `SKILL.md`. Follow its
   link to the exact topic procedure under `.topics/` and read that `SKILL.md`.
   Apply its decision procedure, then consult its supporting article for facts
   and platform qualifications. Topic skills are explicitly read by installed
   file path; automatic nested discovery is not required.
   For platform support, product feasibility, or platform adaptation, first read each relevant
   platform's Getting started procedure, then the specific component or technology
   procedure. Check both the platform model and the surface's support limits.
3. Before finalizing the route, search the [complete topic index](references/topic-index.md)
   for the task's concepts as well as component or framework names. Its trigger
   descriptions connect everyday product requests to Apple's topic names; users
   need not name an Apple framework. Read the owning family and matching topic
   procedure before its supporting reference. Search relevant rows instead of
   loading the full corpus for a narrow question.
   For a screenshot-specific or animated example, also consult its
   [original visual explanation](references/media/index.md) when available.
4. Apply shared guidance and the target platform's documented differences. A
   missing platform subsection means no additional rule is stated; it does not
   prove support, nonapplicability, or identical behavior across platforms.
5. Compose families when the task crosses them: a component can also require
   accessibility, typography, localization, input, or system-experience guidance.
   Map the brief's material decisions to their owning topics. Read the owning
   procedure for each explicit concern, such as privacy or accessibility, as well
   as the affected components; a neighboring procedure's reminder is insufficient.
   Use [platform and task routes](references/platforms-and-tasks.md) when useful.
   In a review, map each supplied control to its candidate component procedure
   even when markup or behavior is missing. Use it to frame inspection questions;
   missing evidence neither proves a defect nor removes that control from scope.

All paths are relative to **this installed package**, not the shell's current
directory. No Python, network, sibling skill installation, or authoring cache is
required to read the guidance.

| Task | Read this topic skill |
|---|---|
| Platform conventions, design principles, games, device adaptation | [Getting started](subskills/apple-hig-getting-started/SKILL.md) |
| Accessibility, typography, color, materials, layout, localization, privacy | [Foundations](subskills/apple-hig-foundations/SKILL.md) |
| Onboarding, loading, search, sharing, accounts, feedback, media, settings | [Patterns](subskills/apple-hig-patterns/SKILL.md) |
| Charts, images, text views, embedded web content | [Content](subskills/apple-hig-content/SKILL.md) |
| Lists, collections, split views, tab views, disclosure and grouping | [Layout and organization](subskills/apple-hig-layout-and-organization/SKILL.md) |
| Buttons, menus, toolbars, menu bar, ornaments and actions | [Menus and actions](subskills/apple-hig-menus-and-actions/SKILL.md) |
| Sidebars, tab bars, search fields, tokens and path controls | [Navigation and search](subskills/apple-hig-navigation-and-search/SKILL.md) |
| Alerts, sheets, popovers, panels, scrolling and windows | [Presentation](subskills/apple-hig-presentation/SKILL.md) |
| Text fields, pickers, sliders, toggles, selection controls | [Selection and input](subskills/apple-hig-selection-and-input/SKILL.md) |
| Progress, activity, gauges and ratings | [Status](subskills/apple-hig-status/SKILL.md) |
| Widgets, Live Activities, notifications, Siri snippets and system surfaces | [System experiences](subskills/apple-hig-system-experiences/SKILL.md) |
| Touch, keyboard, pointer, focus, eyes, gestures, controllers and sensors | [Inputs](subskills/apple-hig-inputs/SKILL.md) |
| Apple Pay, purchases, Siri, VoiceOver, AI, CarPlay and integrations | [Technologies](subskills/apple-hig-technologies/SKILL.md) |

## Perform the requested work

Inspect the supplied brief, flow, code, specification or image before deciding
what is wrong or choosing a framework. Use the user's requested mode:

- **Design:** produce an implementable specification or interaction/state model
  from the topic's decision procedure, with concrete transitions and acceptance
  checks. Connect choices to the user's task and target platform.
- **Implement:** prefer the project's native system components when they supply
  the needed behavior. HIG explains experience requirements; verify API names,
  availability, and code against the appropriate SDK documentation. Make the
  authorized changes in the existing stack; a prose explanation alone does not
  complete an implementation request.
- **Review:** describe the observed problem, its effect, the relevant HIG rule,
  and a concrete correction. Separate source-backed findings from your own
  suggested improvements. Do not invent violations without inspecting evidence.
- **Adapt:** preserve the product task, data and useful state while applying the
  destination platform's interaction model. Patch the supplied artifact or give
  an explicit before/after contract when a design specification is requested.

Topic procedures are framework agnostic. Their worked examples and pseudocode
teach decisions, not a requirement to replace the project's technology. Load
related procedures only for a decision that actually depends on them.

Complete the topic's observable checks and report passed, failed and not executed
separately. Reading a file, citing Apple, or proposing a test does not establish
runtime behavior. Static code or screenshots cannot prove assistive-technology
order, native rendering, physical comfort, haptics, or SDK compilation.

Include official article/section links for material recommendations. Preserve
qualifications such as “consider,” “prefer,” and “avoid”; do not turn design
advice into invented universal requirements. Retain units and platform scope for
numerical specifications. If source passages conflict, describe the conflict
and the conservative application rather than silently changing the source.

## Source boundaries

This is comprehensive local guidance, not a verbatim Apple manual or an SDK API
reference. Original media explanations are supplementary to article references;
the source page remains useful for visual demonstrations. Source snapshots and
review status live in the repository's coverage report, outside ordinary skill
loading. Do not infer that a source has been independently reviewed just because
its local file exists.

Historical `navigation-bars` links now resolve to current Toolbars guidance;
`in-app-purchase` resolves to Apple In-App Purchase. The old Touch Bar and Messages
for Business HIG pages were unavailable at this snapshot. Do not fabricate their
current rules. Translations, archived pages, and complete linked SDK/WWDC libraries
are outside the source boundary.

Platform: iOS. Each typed character starts an untracked request; older responses overwrite newer queries, zero results removes the query and offline search hides local matches. Filters are sticky but not shown.

# Apple HIG: End-to-end behavior and recovery

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Trace the person’s task from entry through completion, cancellation, interruption and recovery. Select the pattern procedure for the actual failure or desired behavior before selecting its controls.
2. Preserve the current work, selection and navigation context across the transitions that matter. Choose interruption or modality according to urgency and task scope, not visual emphasis.
3. For asynchronous or recurring work, separate current progress, eventual result, error recovery and unavailable capability. For audio/video/haptics, specify user control and environmental behavior.
4. Deliver a transition/state specification, a correction to the supplied flow, or ranked findings tied to observed steps. Test alternate exits and resumption, not just the success path.

## Enter the topic procedure

Read the selected topic’s SKILL.md before its supporting guidance. For a review,
inspect actual evidence and return findings; for an implementation request, make
the authorized change; for design or adaptation, produce a usable specification
or patch. Load related topics only when the chosen procedure calls for them.

## Completion evidence

name: apple-hig-searching
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting app, document, or system search strategy, suggestions, scope, history, and indexed-content destinations.
---

# Make the finding route match the content

Read [the searching guide](../../references/searching.md). This workflow is application advice; described Spotlight support specifically concerns iOS/iPadOS/macOS.

Inspect content corpus/metadata, query tasks, local/global scope, history privacy, platform, and create/review/adapt request. Obtain representative queries and actual result/deep-link evidence. Do not invent search relevance or index coverage without data.

Prefer a clear app-wide search while retaining justified local filtering. Give important search a prominent route and explicit scope. Offer useful recents/predictions/completions/filters to reduce entry, allowing history to be cleared because it can expose private intent. Define result identity and destination so selecting a match opens the exact content. For systemwide finding, index descriptive metadata and appropriate custom-file metadata/Quick Look support, respecting the source's platform boundary. Prefer standard Open/Save views for their built-in search instead of rebuilding an incomplete file finder.

Implement query/scope/history/index behavior, provide a corpus-to-query/result specification, or review concrete scope/relevance/privacy defects. Tie suggested filters to actual supported attributes rather than decorative chips that do nothing.

**Worked transformation:** Before: a notes app has three indistinguishable Search boxes, private recent queries cannot be cleared, and Spotlight results open home. Decision: scope and destination do not match finding intent. After: identify one app-wide entry plus clearly local filters, allow history clearing, and route indexed matches to the named note.

Deliver the artifact, scope, suggestions/filters, history policy, metadata, and destinations. Verify representative queries, no results, cleared history, deleted/index-stale content, and external result activation. Fail for unexplained scope, private history with no clearing, or wrong-content links. Index freshness/relevance and native Spotlight execution require actual runtime evidence.

Load [search-fields](../../../apple-hig-navigation-and-search/.topics/apple-hig-search-fields/SKILL.md) for entry placement or [file-management](../apple-hig-file-management/SKILL.md) for document metadata/preview integration.

name: apple-hig-search-fields
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting search entry placement, scope, suggestions, clearing, and token or category refinement.
---

# Make search scope visible before entry

Read [the search-field guide](../../references/search-fields.md). This workflow applies the source; query policy and implementation details remain application decisions.

Inspect searchable content, navigation, platform/input, window sizes, and create/review/adapt mode. Establish global versus local scope, directed lookup versus discovery, and actual query/result behavior. Record placeholder, clear/cancel, suggestions, selected result, and keyboard activation from evidence.

Choose entry placement from scope and priority: local fields beside their content, dedicated discovery areas for browsing, and rapid focused entry for directed lookup. Explain scope in the placeholder and start broad before deliberate narrowing. Offer useful predictive/recent queries and teach token filters through suggestions. Prefer results during typing when feasible, but do not promise instant remote search without data/latency evidence.

Implement the field and query/refinement states or specify placement/scope/focus/result behavior; reviews must trace a misleading query or route. On iPad/Mac coordinate search with split-view selection and resizing. A dedicated iPad discovery area should not unexpectedly open its virtual keyboard. On iOS distinguish persistent search tab from transient button-style search returning to the prior tab. On TV reduce remote entry with suggestions; on watch preserve return after fullscreen Search/Cancel.

**Worked transformation:** Before: `Search` above a sidebar silently searches the whole library, then opens a keyboard over the iPad discovery grid. Decision: placement implies local navigation filtering and automatic focus obscures discovery. After: label a local sidebar search explicitly or move global search to a dedicated area; leave discovery unfocused with a virtual keyboard.

Deliver the changed artifact and scope/focus/clear/selection contract. Verify clearing, category changes, no results, returning from detail, and compact resize. Fail for unexplained scope changes, stale results presented as the current query, or lost result identity. Distinguish native keyboard/input execution from inspected handlers.

Load [searching](../../../apple-hig-patterns/.topics/apple-hig-searching/SKILL.md) for result strategy or [token-fields](../apple-hig-token-fields/SKILL.md) for Mac token entry.

name: apple-hig-loading
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting useful partial content, placeholders, background asset loading, and unavoidable waits.
---

# Keep useful content ahead of the wait

Read [the loading guide](../../references/loading.md). This workflow is application advice; timing and download availability require implementation evidence.

Inspect content dependencies, cached/partial data, asset sizes, initial interaction, platform, and create/review/adapt mode. Separate indispensable work from independent/background work and record measured waits when available. Do not infer duration or success from a skeleton screen.

Show useful structure promptly and replace placeholders as real content arrives. Keep other features usable while loading, retaining known content where appropriate. Schedule large assets nondisruptively with supported background mechanisms instead of blocking every startup. For unavoidable waits beyond a moment, communicate ongoing work and estimate only when measurable. Match optional engaging content to duration without a repetitive loop that disguises a stall. Games can use thematic loading, but truthful status/recovery still matters. On watch immediate content is preferable; brief indicators beat blank screens, while longer waits should not encourage wrist watching.

Implement content/dependency/loading states or provide a partial-content/placeholder/progress specification; reviews identify exact unnecessary blocking and misleading-placeholder defects. Define error/retry/available-data behavior according to the task rather than leaving a permanent fake skeleton.

**Worked transformation:** Before: a catalog blocks browsing until all preview videos download and replaces cached products with blank placeholders on refresh. Decision: independent assets should not remove useful content. After: show cached/current product information promptly, load previews in background, and give honest localized wait/retry feedback only for content that actually needs it.

Deliver the artifact, readiness/partial-content policy, asset schedule, and wait resolution. Verify slow/offline, partial success, refresh with existing data, retry, and completion. Fail for unnecessary whole-screen blocking, placeholders mistaken for real values, or an unresolved wait with no recovery. Report measured runtime timing separately from a proposed loading design.

Use [launching](../apple-hig-launching/SKILL.md) for startup or [progress-indicators](../../../apple-hig-status/.topics/apple-hig-progress-indicators/SKILL.md) for measurement and cancellation details.

# Searching Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/searching) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. Support finding content in the app, document, and system. Recents, predictions, completions, corrections, attribute filters, and scopes can reduce effort. Spotlight on iOS/iPadOS/macOS can expose indexed content without first opening the app. ## Best practices Give important search a prominent toolbar or dedicated tab position. Prefer one clear app-wide search, retaining local filtering when distinct sections justify it. Communicate scope with placeholder, title, or scope control. Offer useful suggestions before/during entry. Treat search history as potentially private and let people clear it. ## Systemwide search Index app content with descriptive metadata. Custom file formats need metadata import support for Spotlight. Contextual commands can initiate an advanced Spotlight query and show relevant filtered results. Prefer system Open/Save views for their built-in systemwide search, and supply Quick Look generation for custom document previews. ## Platform considerations The source adds no separate rules for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, or watchOS; systemwide Spotlight support described here specifically applies to iOS/iPadOS/macOS. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Search fields](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/search-fields) #### Developer documentation — Core Spotlight #### Videos ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: June 8, 2026, June 9, 2025.

# Search fields Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/search-fields) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. A search field combines editable query text with a Search glyph, clearing, and a scope-explaining placeholder. Scope bars and tokens can refine the query; entry placement depends on the platform and search's role. ## Best practices Explain searchable content in the placeholder. Prefer updating results during typing where possible. Offer recent or predictive queries to reduce effort, prioritize relevant results, and group results when it improves navigation. Add filtering where it helps people narrow the result set. ## Scope bars and tokens A scope bar switches among clearly defined categories or breadths. Start broad to show the available result context and let people narrow deliberately. A token encapsulates a meaningful term or attribute as a selectable, editable unit, such as one contact or a photo filter. Pair available tokens with suggestions to teach these less-visible options. ## Platform considerations visionOS has no additional rules in this source. ### iOS Search can be a tab, a toolbar item, or inline with content. Choose its placement from the scope, navigation structure, and priority. #### Search as a tab A standard search tab opens a landing page with a field above useful categories, suggestions, or discovery content. A separate button-style search tab immediately focuses the field and opens the keyboard; leaving that transient search returns to the prior tab. Choose the former for browsing rich content and the latter for fast directed lookup. #### Search in a toolbar Bottom toolbars can contain an expanded field or a search button according to available width. Activation moves the field above the keyboard. Top/navigation toolbars use a button that opens a field above the keyboard, or at the top when bottom space is insufficient. Favor reachable bottom placement when space permits, even as the toolbar's only control. Use top placement when bottom content serves an important immediate purpose or there is no bottom toolbar. #### Search as an inline field Place a field beside its content when location should communicate local rather than global scope, especially when the app has multiple searches. At the top of a list, put it above that list and consider pinning it to the top toolbar during scrolling. ### iPadOS, macOS Keep counterpart apps' search patterns consistent. Trailing toolbar search suits searching across split-view columns and preserving a result selection beside its detail, or filtering content in the detail area. Search at the top of a sidebar suits filtering navigation or finding nested settings while leaving a rich detail view distinct. A sidebar or tab-bar item can instead open a dedicated discovery area with space for suggestions and categories. In a dedicated search area, immediate focus can speed entry and reveal the field. On iPad with only a virtual keyboard, leave it unfocused so the keyboard does not unexpectedly cover discovery content. Account for fluid resizing: a compact iPad layout may need search above the relevant content-list column instead of in the full-width toolbar. ### tvOS The search screen combines a keyboard with customizable results below it. Reduce remote typing through popular, contextual, and recent suggestions. ### watchOS Activating search opens a fullscreen text-entry control. The app returns to the search field after Search or Cancel. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Searching](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/searching) [Token fields](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/token-fields) #### Developer documentation — SwiftUI — SwiftUI — UIKit — UIKit — AppKit #### Videos ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: June 8, 2026, June 9, 2025, September 12, 2023, June 5, 2023.

# Loading Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/loading) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. Load content without interrupting useful interaction, ideally before waiting becomes noticeable. ## Best practices Show useful scaffolding, graphics, or placeholders promptly and replace them as real content arrives. Continue loading in the background while people use other features. For unavoidable waits, offer relevant tips or engaging content matched to the likely duration without repetitive loops. Schedule large assets with background-download mechanisms after install, during updates, or other nondisruptive periods to improve installation and startup. ## Showing progress If loading lasts more than a moment or two, show that work continues and give an estimate where possible. Use determinate progress for measurable work and indeterminate for unknown duration. Games can use a thematic custom loading view where standard progress styling would feel out of place. ## Platform considerations No additional iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, or visionOS rules are specified. ### watchOS Prefer immediate content and avoid wait indicators when possible. For a brief unavoidable second or two, an indicator is preferable to a blank display. Application advice: longer waits should not encourage prolonged wrist watching. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Launching](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/launching) [Progress indicators](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/progress-indicators) #### Developer documentation #### Videos ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: June 9, 2025, June 10, 2024.

item.text: The supplied spec identifies four failures: stale responses, query loss, hidden local matches offline, and invisible filters. I’ll define a tracked query lifecycle, keep local search independent of network availability, and make the active scope visible. Request timing and matching rules will be explicit product decisions, not claims about HIG requirements.

# iPhone offline document archive — revised search specification

Platform: iOS on iPhone. This is a behavior contract for the existing archive, independent of implementation framework. Search must remain useful without a network connection.

## Entry, scope, and filters

| Apply, remove, clear filters; begin fresh session | Count/results track visible refinements; fresh session has none. |
| Search and open fixture documents in airplane mode; lose/recover connectivity mid-query | Same local matches remain available; network state cannot erase them. |
| Slow search, partial index, index failure, retry | Editing remains usable; partial coverage is qualified; failure differs from empty results; retry has a new generation. |
| Open D1 and return; delete D1 before selection | Normal return restores query/filters/position with current-index validation; deletion gives unavailable recovery without opening D2. |
| Empty or whitespace input, repeated terms, case variants, equal titles | Defined matching, empty-query behavior, and stable identity/order hold. |
| Keyboard, narrow iPhone layout, long query/filter labels, assistive technology | Entry, query editing, clear/refinement actions and result identity remain operable and understandable; validate on implementation. |

## Audit and limits

Passed by static document inspection: interface.md now defines corrections for all four supplied failures and covers query lifecycle, scope, focus/clear, selection, zero results, offline/partial content, retry, and return. The worked example is consistent with the revised contract. No failed runtime checks are reported because none ran.

Read locally, in order: installed apple-hig root SKILL.md; interface.md; Patterns and Navigation and search family SKILL.md files; relevant searching/search-fields/loading rows of references/topic-index.md; each selected topic SKILL.md; then the three corresponding source guides. Each instruction/source file was read with a separate cat or rg command using its installed package path. The topic index’s iCloud route was not selected because no iCloud or synchronization integration is supplied. No platform adaptation, Spotlight, new history, or framework replacement is proposed.

Not executed: application code changes/builds, SDK compilation, device/simulator/GUI interactions, native keyboard behavior, offline execution, performance measurements, index coverage/relevance validation, or accessibility execution. Only interface.md and local installed guidance were supplied as evidence; there is no corpus, implementation, screenshot, or test harness. The local guides identify a 2026-10-25 snapshot and do not establish independent review or runtime conformance. Official links above are attribution only; no web browsing occurred. The delivered repair is a revised specification, not proof that an app implements it.
